sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved; insufficient evidence for a new-purchase ranking. Flywings operates a real, profitable safety/emergency training facility, but the transition from owned equipment to long foreign-currency simulator leases changes both capital economics and downside. The dated ₹281.95 close values 10,177,128 shares at ₹286.94 crore. FY2026 group revenue ₹24.6390 crore and PAT ₹11.6448 crore are reported, not proof of cash compounding: the latest annual report gives CFO ₹2.5827 crore, versus ₹6.0177 crore in the earlier corrected results. The later filing repairs much of the cash roll-forward but does not settle all consolidation/accounting issues.

BQS NS, GQS NS, IAS NS. CAP, CASH and BAL are not neutral scores of 5; evidence is insufficient. G1/G2/G3 are unresolved holds; G4 conditional. There is no evidenced issuer-fraud conclusion and no asserted current default. A conditional five-year base illustration returns 10.10%, below the 15% hurdle; it is not a supported forecast or price target. Missing lease/cash evidence and the unfunded stress case are more consequential than headline PAT, a reputed airline client or a broad aviation-growth story. This is a research hold, not a trade instruction.

sections.title: Research Header and Gate Register
sections.text:
Company: Flywings Simulator Training Centre Limited; NSE Emerge symbol FWSTC, ISIN INE0SQZ01015. Sector: aviation safety/emergency and simulator training, with ancillary drone/MRO/flying-school proposals. Cutoff 20 October 2026; information accessed 21 October but only dated pre-cutoff issuer events used. Quote is official 19 October close ₹281.95; last-traded ₹277 is a different field, not substituted. Reporting is Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not Ind AS. Latest annual report dated September 2026 anchors 31 March 2026 consolidated accounts; standalone and restated variants are separately retained.

Horizon:19 October 2026–19 October 2031; hurdle 15% nominal pre-tax INR equity return. Return is after modeled corporate tax, before investor tax; no distributions assumed. Market-cap/share-count and lot verified in exchange files. Promoter holding is last retrieved March declaration, not asserted current October ownership. No newer verified dilution instrument was found; authorized-capital increase approved September is not issued dilution.

G1 Hold: clarify guarantee/RPT/pledge/pay perimeter; legal allegations are not adjudicated issuer misconduct. G2 Hold: obtain auditor-endorsed cash flow/consolidation reconciliation, including comparative PBT and intercompany elimination. G3 Hold: obtain signed lease schedule, bank/lien certificates, NCD repayment and fully funded cost-to-complete. G4 Conditional: check live restrictions, order-book depth and actual whole-lot execution before implementation. A G3 hold alone does not disqualify business-quality ranking; here missing CAP/CASH/BAL and independent G2 reliability do.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 4; MOAT 5; REV 8; DUR 5; CAP NS; CASH NS; BAL NS; EXEC 4; EARN 4; R NS; D NS; P NS; L 4. Full evidence and reasons are in factor_audit. Revenue scoring uses 33.18% 3Y standalone growth, a one-point sustained-trajectory reduction from 9 to 8, then the short-history ceiling of 8; pandemic growth is not rewarded. Earnings and cash factors are distinct. Liquidity starts at 5 under the 6.30-day band and is reduced once for documented lot/zero-session/surveillance frictions.

BQS known weighted contribution 3.58, coverage 70%, possible bound 3.88–6.58; GQS known contribution 4.80, coverage 75%, bound 5.05–7.30; IAS known contribution 0.40, coverage 10%, bound 1.30–9.40. These are mathematical bounds, not statistical confidence intervals or point estimates. Q in IAS remains missing because final BQS is NS. No weight redistribution, guessed neutral factors or hidden haircut. Raw/final scores stay null; no governance, funding or persistent-CAP/CASH numeric override applied. Growth Quality Score is GQS, not governance quality. Ranking excluded for insufficient critical evidence and G2 hold, not because G3 is merely unresolved.

sections.title: Business Model and Value Chain
sections.text:
The established Gurugram Safety and Emergency Procedures facility supplies training infrastructure: aircraft-door/cabin emergency trainers, evacuation and water-survival facilities, and classrooms. Airlines can bring their own instructors; the facility is not simply selling pilot licenses. Mandatory recurrent checks support repeat training. Recognition occurs when service obligations are fulfilled/accepted; repeat demand is not the same as cash collection. FY2026 revenue note separates cabin crew ₹22.6783 crore, pilot ₹1.6342 crore, MRO ₹0.1992 crore and drone ₹0.1273 crore. Cabin training is therefore the current economic engine, not four already-operating full-flight simulators.

The company has a drone subsidiary and roughly 49.65% associate Ambitions Flying Club. Mumbai/Panvel plans involve two initial A320 full-flight simulators on 10-year foreign-currency leases, with other equipment/verticals discussed later. Do not mistake management’s four-unit/vertical potential or the Gurugram approval for commissioned Mumbai FFS capacity. Dholera is a conditional AAI LOI plus an upcoming-facility announcement; no revenue or investment return is booked in this review. Proposed transport/logistics objects broaden optionality but also capital-allocation risk; shareholder approval was still future at cutoff.

sections.title: Moat, Customers and Competition
sections.text:
Mechanism→evidence→durability→failure: specialized installed SEP equipment and airline workflow integration→existing airline business and repeat training→moderate replacement/qualification friction→customers internalize training, shift to a rival or terminate. DGCA approval is a threshold to operate, not exclusive legal protection. The prospectus’s detailed FY2025 table gives largest customer ₹6.5987 crore/32.65% and top 10₹18.1861 crore/89.98%; the 92.64% risk-summary figure conflicts and is not silently substituted. FY2024 and FY2023 top 10 concentration was 94.37% and 93.18%. Detailed concentration is high even if clients are reputable. Contracts may terminate on notice without meaningful penalty; no current customer renewal, cohort retention or net revenue retention series establishes strong pricing power.

Recurring aviation-training demand creates an accessible market, but issuer market share with a defensible denominator is ND. Public rivals include CAE and FSTC; Air India’s 21 September release described 21 simulators being installed in its academy, not 21 already operational. CAE’s dated FY2026 release reports 70% civil-training utilization,16% reported/18.6% adjusted operating margin and fleet optimization. These are not direct margin or valuation comparables, but contradict the assumption that all new Indian capacity automatically fills 85–90%. FSTC’s undated website is used qualitatively only. Rival capacity, airline bargaining power, approval timing, instructor availability and equipment uptime limit a strong-moat conclusion.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Earnings Bridge
sections.text:
Historical revenue records are retained rather than spliced: original standalone FY2021₹1.4896 crore and FY2022₹1.4367 crore; prospectus-restated standalone FY2023₹10.3765 crore and FY2024₹22.2028 crore; FY2025 standalone ₹20.2105 crore; FY2026 standalone ₹24.5117 crore. The 3Y CAGR is 33.18%; FY2024 jump was followed by FY2025−8.97% and FY2026+21.28%, not uninterrupted hypergrowth. The 5Y 75.09% CAGR begins in pandemic disruption and is unsuitable as the scoring anchor.10Y, post-FY2026 TTM and latest comparable interim cash flow are ND. Absolute revenue addition in FY2026 standalone is ₹4.3012 crore. A disclosed volume/price/customer bridge is incomplete; do not call all group growth organic.

Latest annual-report group revenue ₹20.2660→24.6390 crore grew 21.58%; operational EBITDA excluding all other income ₹13.8655→15.4152 crore grew 11.18%; EBIT ₹12.9967→14.1627 crore grew 8.97%. Employee and other operating costs absorbed growth. Group reported PAT ₹10.3222→11.6448 crore grew 12.81%; other income fell ₹3.4329→1.6703 crore and included interest, rent and unbilled service income. Prior-period charge ₹0.0526 crore, policy reversal ₹0.4324 crore and associate profit ₹0.2107 crore are separated. No unsupported write-off add-back is used.

Core NOPAT at an analytical 25% tax is ₹9.7475→10.6220 crore, not audited normalized PAT. Current-end-share core EPS falls about 17.93% after the fresh issue; this is the proper dilution warning, although the IPO capital may not yet be productive. Reported EPS denominators describe end-period shares as weighted averages and FY2025 EPS does not cleanly reconcile; no false EPS CAGR. Gross profit/value added is ND. financial_history.json contains levels, margins, CFO, capex and FCF with original/restated scope and missing data explicit.

sections.title: Growth Runway and Incremental Capital Economics
sections.text:
Reinvestment is the central unresolved issue. Original IPO equipment objects of ₹35.3398 crore included cabin-evacuation equipment ₹6.9393 crore,6 DOF ₹6.0843 crore and fixed-base A320₹22.3162 crore. May shareholders approved a change toward two full-flight A320 leases,10-year tenure, upfront/downpayment plus rentals and Mumbai location; CEET remains Gurugram. That substitutes operating/FX commitments for owned-asset economics, not free capacity. The May notice reports machine utilization nil, whereas the later annual report’s March table reports ₹6.6601 crore spent/₹28.6706 crore unspent; the timeline and ₹0.0091 crore table arithmetic difference require reconciliation.

June call targets: two initial simulators; ready-for-training by end December 2026, revenue from January 2027; no signed Mumbai customer contracts yet; rent starts only after RFT/installation conditions described in the call. Monthly USD 100,000 was stated without an adequately clear combined-versus-per-machine scope. Formal notice flags EUR risk. Full signed currency/escalator/deposit/termination schedules are absent. Management’s USD 3 m-per-unit revenue/55% EBITDA and high utilization are assertions, not mature cohort results. Jan 2027 was not yet a missed deadline at cutoff.

CAP is NS. No comparable 3Y/5Y incremental-ROIC denominator can reliably isolate operating capital from RPT, property/associate investments, changed consolidation and IPO cash. financial_history.json displays a mechanical funding-residual ratio only to show why it is not valid causal return evidence. Existing utilization/margin gains do not prove new capital earns that ratio. No commissioned full-flight unit’s realized hours, rate, lease-adjusted contribution, maintenance, collections or cash-on-cash return is available. A14–18% post-tax nominal INR operating cost-of-capital range is an explicit analytical benchmark, not a sourced company WACC or the 15% equity hurdle.

Prospective model:2× 8000 hours×₹35000 gives ₹56 crore full-capacity annual revenue. With 20% variable cost, combined USD 1.2 m annual rent at ₹90 and ₹3 crore fixed cost, EBITDA break-even utilization is 30.8%; stress using per-machine rent USD 2.4 m, ₹100 FX, ₹30000/hour,30% variable cost and ₹4 crore fixed cost needs 83.3%. These exclude tax, funding, capital and maintenance effects and are not substitutes for realized CAP evidence. Dholera, MRO and logistics have no independently funded cohort model; no free terminal value assigned.

sections.title: Governance, Ownership and Minority Protection
sections.text:
Rupal Sanjay Mandavia’s last retrieved March holding is 6,093,414 shares/59.87%; public 40.13%,358 holders. FY2025 bonus 110:1 is not an economic fresh issuance. IPO fresh 2,512,800 shares increased shares 32.79%; old owners retain 75.31% before OFS transfers.₹47.9945 crore fresh proceeds belong to issuer; ₹9.0534 crore OFS belongs to seller. March holdings disclose no warrants/convertibles/ESOP or encumbrance; October exchange shares remain 10,177,128. September authorized-capital increase creates capacity, not actual dilution.

A material conflict remains: annual debt note says 13% NCD ₹2.4791 crore secured by 1,472,982 promoter shares, about 24.17% of promoter holding/14.47% of total, while March holdings say no pledge. The note’s 5 October 2024/24-month term implies October 2026 maturity; cutoff redemption/release not verified. Do not assume a default or clean pledge position. March RPT and contingent-guarantee records must likewise be reconciled with the June call’s denial of association/liability with Big Charter. MD receivable, salary advance and listing-expense recoverable require settlement evidence; high promoter ownership does not resolve the conflict.

FY2026 MD remuneration ₹1.20 crore, including ₹0.24 crore excess, was subsequently ratified at September 29 AGM. Interested promoter votes were excluded on the relevant resolutions; this is meaningful process remediation. It does not reconcile the ₹0.8294 crore remuneration component in group employee expenses, ₹0.47 crore salary advance or ₹1.25 crore listing-expense recoverable. Issue-expense cash ₹8.3463 crore also exceeds ₹7.9713 crore budget; OFS/issuer allocation needs proof. Unmodified statutory audit, approvals and reported regular loan receipts are counter-evidence; none automatically proves all balances sound.

Legal attribution: prospectus records a 20 March 2024 FIR 0130/2024 lodged by Vishok Mansingh of Vman Aero against Big Charter Private Limited and named directors Sanjay Natvarlal Mandavia, Rupal Sanjay Mandavia and Chander Bahadur over alleged escrow transactions ₹8.4573 crore. The company states Rupal was nonexecutive, resigned 2 January 2024, anticipatory bail was granted, and no adverse finding existed at prospectus date; quashing proceedings were pending. Post-prospectus court outcome is unverified. This is not a finding against the listed issuer. October 15 clarification expressly says Sanjay was never CEO; this review identifies him only as a call participant. GOV 4/G1 Hold reflect disclosure/stewardship evidence, not guilt by association.

sections.title: Financial Forensics, Cash and Funding
sections.text:
Latest group FY2026 CFO ₹2.5827 crore/PAT ₹11.6448 crore=22.18%; FY2025 latest comparative CFO ₹6.9415 crore/PAT ₹10.3222 crore; two-year conversion 43.36%. Three comparable reliable years are ND, not manufactured by mixing prospectus CFO 9.0694 with annual figures. FY2026 standalone CFO 4.5110/PAT 11.4340 is a different perimeter and cannot replace group cash realization. Reported group FCF proxy 2.5827−physical capex 0.2645=₹2.3182 crore, before expansion advances, investments, collateral and financing. Depreciation is not a maintenance-capex estimate.

Annual cash bridge: PBT 15.4185+DA 1.2525−interest income 1.2453+gratuity 0.0703+associate adjustment 0.2107+finance 0.7942=16.5009 crore before working capital. WC movements total−9.8618 crore, notably short advances−4.9387, other current liabilities−4.0314, receivables−1.2619 and provisions+2.1032; tax−4.0565 yields 2.5827. Capex itself does not explain weak CFO. The positive associate-profit adjustment, deferred-tax/current-provision treatment and retained subsidiary/RPT balances remain questionable classifications, not asserted fraud. Receivable end-days improve 151.56→143.36, but older-than 6 months increases 20.94%→32.43%, so headline DSO improvement is insufficient.

September 3 CFO 6.0177 becomes 2.5827 via associate-adjustment change−0.5835 and noncurrent-liability change−2.8515. Earlier CFF 38.8000 becomes 31.2478, principally listing-fee correction 0.7942→8.3463. Earlier net cash 28.9519 cannot reconcile opening 5.6907 toclosing 23.6553: error 10.9873. The annual cash bridge reconciles within ₹0.0001 crore rounding. Remaining issues: comparative CFS starts PAT 10.3222 labelled PBT vs P&L 14.6796; copied/comparative receivable movements; subsidiary negative reserves ₹45.64 lakh considered in other current assets; intercompany/RPT elimination; FY2025 PPE/cash flow and EPS comparability. A later date is not economic resolution by itself.

Student training advance ₹0.50 crore is explicitly an advance PAID under annual Note 17(short-term asset), so the ONWC model adds it rather than subtracting customer fees. The prospectus PDFp 250 RPT table’s advance-received wording for Ambitions requires counterparty/settlement reconciliation, not a unilateral sign reversal. March asset/funding map: equity 89.8612, funded debt 13.8031, bank/cash 23.6553, noncurrent FD 17.0944 and DSRA 1.0625, associate/property 27.1007, short RPT loans 10.4269, capital advance 6.7269, aircraft advance 1.0884, tax provision 6.0031 and TDSasset 1.7929 crore.₹7 crore Big Charter guarantee and ₹0.394 crore TDS demand are separate contingent claims. Claims against company are unascertainable. Auditor also reports overdue income tax ₹2.2945 crore; overlap with tax provision is unproven, base assumes overlap and stress adds it once. Do not call all cash/FD unrestricted or loans liquid.

The annual model’s opening-claim ledger treats debt/current maturities once, embedded payables via ONWC once, earmarked IPO balance as a purpose within bank cash rather than additional cash, old advances as already paid, RPT recoveries only when realized, collateral only when released, taxes once and lease rent in both operating earnings and cash. No leased-simulator purchase or separate lease-PV debt is double deducted against post-rent EV. Actual October cash and full commitments remain unverified; G3 Hold rather than evidenced funding failure.

sections.title: Valuation, Scenarios and Price-Implied Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹281.95, market cap ₹286.94 crore, current-share reported P/E 24.64×, core-NOPAT price multiple 27.01× and reported P/B 3.19×. These use disclosed March figures and are diagnostics, not a reliable bargain signal. A naive net-cash EV ignores earmarks, liens, future leases, guarantees and nonoperating assets. No pure listed peer has sufficiently matched mix/scale/accounting for a defensible relative target. High peer adjusted margins are not imported.

model.py runs annual sales, post-rent EBITDA, depreciation, interest, tax, working capital, capex, cash, debt and shares for exactly 5 years. Opening 31 March 2026 cash is adjusted by explicit illustrative stub spending, not represented as 19 Oct actual cash. All scenarios repay ₹13.8031 crore opening debt in Y 1 and explicitly handle old taxes, collateral and claims. Upfront remaining project budgets are assumptions anchored to disputed IPO unspent disclosure.₹8000 hours capacity per simulator, hourly pricing, utilization, tax 25%, legacy margins, maintenance and multiples are analyst assumptions. Depreciation on project spend is an explicit 10% analytical proxy, not evidence that leased simulators are owned or that all downpayments are depreciable. Terminal multiples apply to post-rent earnings and assume continuing capacity; remaining lease term and renewal economics are not independently valued. Signed leases are absent; USD denomination from call and EUR risk in notice are not a verified single contractual schedule.

Base: legacy growth 5% then 8%,55% legacy EBITDA, two simulators at 40/50/60/65/70% utilization and half first-year operation, initial ₹35000/hour, combined USD 1.2 m annual rent, ₹90/USD escalating 3%, ₹28.6706 crore project budget including stub, ONWC 38% ofsales, terminal 10× post-rent EBITDA. Y 5 sales ₹77.63 crore, EBITDA ₹37.50 crore, terminal cash ₹73.81 crore, discounted nonoperating assets ₹15.44 crore, terminal equity ₹464.26 crore/₹456.18 per share; illustrative IRR 10.10%. No dividends or further issuance. Mathematical funding works only under these assumptions; not a supported R score.

Bull: stronger pricing/utilization and 13× terminal multiple give ₹889.51 terminal/25.83% IRR. Bear: weak legacy/customer demand, delayed capacity, low utilization, per-machine rental interpretation, adverse FX, high WC and guarantee call create first-year ₹9.05 crore shortfall and cumulative ₹92.08 crore deficit. Principal bear terminal equity/price/IRR are null, not a fake financed endpoint. A separately labeled hypothetical 50%-discount equity rescue raises ₹94.08 crore, increases shares to 1.6850 crore and yields ₹3.43 terminal/−58.60% IRR to the existing share; financing is not committed or recommended.

Post-shortfall bear rows are an unfunded diagnostic continuation only, not an executable business path. The model includes 12/15/18% entry-hurdle prices, utilization× terminal multiple and rent× FX grids, and full linked reverse solve. Base-derived 15% entry price is ₹226.80 (12%₹258.85;18%₹199.40), conditional illustrations not buy levels. Holding base assumptions and 10× exit multiple requires roughly 88.96% terminal utilization, scaling the entire annual ramp, to earn 15% at ₹281.95. That is demanding against the absent contracts/approval and cost ambiguity, but does not establish a supported P score. No probability-weighted target, expected return or IAS is computed.

sections.title: Strongest Bear Case and Falsification
sections.text:
The decisive variable is lease-adjusted, collected contribution from the new Mumbai units, not stated aviation demand. Customer hesitation or a delayed RFT leaves an infrastructure bill before dependable cash generation. Once lease obligations activate, utilization below break-even, INR depreciation, weak collections and an adverse guarantee outcome can consume March liquidity; related-party assets may not be monetizable when needed. The linked stress demonstrates a funding gap, not an actual insolvency finding.

Strongest evidence against an excessively negative interpretation: the established SEP facility generates substantial operating earnings, airlines require recurrent training, the auditor’s opinion is unmodified, Gurugram renewal is current, IPO variation and remuneration received shareholder approval, and much of the September cash flow error is arithmetically traceable. A complete reconciliation plus enforceable leases, funded cash budget, Mumbai certification, paying customers and credible unit economics could materially improve classification.

Thesis-break evidence would be proven material diversion/irrecoverable related-party loss, unreconciled bank cash, unfinanceable legal obligations, or persistent lease-adjusted negative unit contribution after a fair ramp. One price decline or a normal commissioning delay alone is not such evidence. Conversely, share-price strength, a Dholera photograph, an LOI or broad object-clause expansion does not clear the hold. No claim is made that the market has overlooked this public information.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Speculative / unsupported, not a multibagger recommendation. Over five years 5× requires 37.97% annualized price growth and 10× 58.49%, before investor tax. With unchanged shares, target equity values are ₹1434.72 crore and ₹2869.44 crore. At 20× P/E these require common earnings ₹71.74 crore/₹143.47 crore; at 30% net margin, revenue ₹239.12 crore/₹478.24 crore, roughly 9.70×/19.41× FY2026 reported group sales. At a lower 15× multiple required revenues rise to ₹318.83 crore/₹637.65 crore.25% additional shares would increase required earnings/revenue a further 25%; dividends would be separate.

This is dimensional feasibility arithmetic, not a funded forecast. Current two-unit capacity at ₹35000/hour is ₹56 crore full-capacity annual simulator revenue before variability, plus the legacy business. Achieving the 5×/10× requirements therefore needs additional capacity/products, commissioning, margin durability and substantial funding beyond the disclosed initial two units, or substantially different pricing/valuation. No verified accessible-market share, realized new-unit reinvestment return or fully financed expansion path supports that jump. The bull five-year annual model itself produces only about 3.15× price, not 5×. No precise success probability assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring and Evidence Needed
sections.text:
1. Cashflow/consolidation: baseline Sept 3 CFO 6.0177 vsannual 2.5827; obtain signed auditor reconciliation at next results. Any unresolved material bank/intercompany mismatch keeps G2 Hold; correction alone needs full balance-sheet tie-out.
2. Mumbai RFT/commissioning: baseline June targetend December 2026/January 2027 revenue; obtain unit-specific certificate, installation acceptance and first paid hours. A missed target prompts review; recurring unproductive lease cash burn is the economic break.
3. Lease schedule: baseline 10 years, unclear USD 100000/month perimeter and EUR risk; obtain rent per unit, currencies/escalators, deposits, start triggers, termination and maintenance. Economics near per-machine stress break-even 83% require substantially stronger contracted utilization.
4. Funding: baseline Marchcash 23.6553/FD 17.0944/DSRA 1.0625, debt 13.8031; verify October bank/liens, NCD redemption and committed completion costs. Unfunded essential obligations would change G3 from Hold to Fail only when evidenced.
5. Related-party claims: baseline guarantee 7 and RPTloans 10.4269; obtain named-counterparty roll-forward, repayment and legal release. Material unexplained increase or nonrecoverability raises governance/capital loss risk.
6. Receivables: baseline 32.43% older 6 months despite 143.36 enddays; review customer-level collections and ageing next financials. Further migration without receipts matters more than sales growth.
7. Proceeds/ownership: reconcile Marchspend versus Maynil andissue/OFS expenses; confirm pledge release/current encumbrance and actual issued capital after authorized-capital increase. New instruments require fully diluted model rerun.
8. Capital allocation: Nov 5 EGM proposed objects, conditional Dholera LOI, no funded returns; obtain budgets before giving incremental growth credit. Unfunded unrelated diversification would worsen execution/funding assessment.
9. Trading: refresh actual NSE lot, REG 1 status,60 session turnover andlivebid/ask before any implementation. Do not annualize the recentvolume spike or assume all reference exits fit whole lots.
Cadence is a research recommendation only; no reminders, trades or monitoring automation created.

sections.title: Classification, Ranking and Action Logic
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved / insufficient critical evidence. This is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate, not an actionable value classification and not Avoid — governance. BQS/GQS/IAS are NS; price-sensitive R/D/P cannot be supported. Do not sort the company by a fabricated 0,5 or capped 3; preserve nulls and missing-factor intervals. G3 Hold alone is not a business-quality exclusion. Here quality ranks are unavailable because CAP/CASH/BAL lack defensible evidence, and IAS additionally fails the independent G2 reliability requirement.

Analysis is completed to the available evidence, with explicit holds rather than a claim that missing documents were reviewed. Re-entry to ranking needs a reliable financial perimeter, full lease/funding and exposure reconciliations, and mature incremental-unit evidence for CAP or an alternative truly comparable capital-return history. If those arrive, recompute factors and scenarios independently, without forcing a prior preferred rank. The ₹5 lakh reference is only for comparable liquidity testing, not a recommended allocation.

sections.title: Sources, Reproducibility and Confidence
sections.text:
Primary evidence is preserved with URLs, document dates, precise PDF/field locators and SHA 256 hashes in source_ledger.json; evidence_ledger.json distinguishes Vverified disclosure, Ccalculation, Aassumption and Uunresolved. Downloaded report text is supplemented by OCR and retained images for scanned financial notes. Original documents, not OCR alone, control where values conflict. The source list includes dated competitor evidence; the undated FSTC site is qualitative and outside the exact cutoff only as an access snapshot.

Reproduce: python 3 financial_analysis.py; python 3 model.py; python 3 liquidity/extract.py; python 3 build_research.py; python 3 qa.py from the package directory. All scripts use Python standard library for calculations; downloads/OCR require separate tools. Full package includes all 60 NSEarchives and 19 October security/regulatory files. Compact Essentials includes canonical JSON, model/financial results, extracted session ledger, evidence/source ledger and QA but omits large raw sources. No external database or mutable live price is required to recalculate stored evidence.

Confidence: identity/high; dates/primary disclosed figures/high; economic normalization/low-medium; consolidation/cash reliability/low; forward valuation/low; historical liquidity/high, execution depth/unknown. Unavailable: current bank confirmations, full executed lease terms, NCD redemption, new-unit cohorts, clean intercompany elimination, current litigation disposition, verified post-March shareholding/encumbrance and Mumbai RFT/contracts. Returned October EGM file is only acover; Dholera purported LOI annexure lacks commercial terms. No claim these records do not exist. No trading or external outreach performed.

GOV.reason: Commercial RPT and guarantee exposure, contradictory public perimeter, pledge and pay-accounting gaps weaken minority protection. Approvals and unmodified audit are counter-evidence; no established issuer fraud or evidenced severe governance failure.

MOAT.reason: Installed specialized SEP infrastructure and airline workflows give moderate switching friction. Certification is necessary rather than exclusive; concentrated customers, termination rights and competing/airline-owned capacity prevent durable high-moat claims.

REV.reason: Comparable 3Y standalone 33.18% CAGR starts at 9; sustained recent deceleration versus FY2024 level and FY2025 contraction justify net−1 to 8, then the short-history ceiling 8 applies. Pandemic-distorted 75.09% 5Y not scored; revenue growth, not margin expansion.

DUR.reason: Recurrent training is durable; issuer-specific runway depends on unsigned demand conversion, Mumbai approval, lease economics and disciplined diversification. Large aviation TAM is not issuer revenue.

CAP.reason: No reliable comparable incremental capital denominator or realized newly commissioned unit/cohort returns. Current ROCE and prospective simulator break-even do not establish incremental returns; NS, not neutral 5.

CASH.reason: Reported 22.18% FY26 and 43.36% two-year cash conversion are warning signals, but conflicting CFO, comparative and consolidation treatment prevent a reliable canonical factor; NS, not an arbitrary low score.

BAL.reason: Cash/deposit availability, full foreign-currency lease obligations, NCD redemption and guarantees not adequately reconciled. A reported net-cash snapshot is insufficient for survival scoring; NS.

EXEC.reason: Existing SEP operation and renewal are real delivery. IPO plan changed materially, corrections recurred and new-unit commissioning/contracts are unproven. Jan 2027 target has not yet been missed at cutoff.

EARN.reason: Core EBIT grew 8.97% against group revenue 21.58%; nonoperating income and tax/prior-period items matter, and current-end-share core earnings fell 17.93% after issuance. Uneven per-share progression; cash issues scored separately.

R.reason: Conditional illustrative base 10.10% is not a defensible forecast with unresolved G2/G3. Do not convert it to a supported R band; no expected-return ranking.

D.reason: No reliable asset availability or quantified lease/litigation downside floor. Rescue economics are diagnostic, not a probability-backed downside estimate.

P.reason: Price reverse-solve requires 89% terminal simulator utilization under optimistic lease interpretation, but contractual/per-share basis remains insufficient for a canonical expectations score.

L.reason: 6.30-day continuous ₹5 L/5% 60-session exit starts at 5; reduce one point for lot granularity,9 zero days and verified STASM 1. Recent 20-session improvement is disclosed, not substituted for 60-session base.

opening_claim_mapping: Current and noncurrent funded debt
Paid once in model year 1; includes current maturities and subsidiary extra ₹2.7037 crore. No terminal debt deduction thereafter.
March noncurrent FD
Included once in opening pool; assumed ₹3.6 crore restricted withheld and conditionally released upon debt repayment; exact lien/maturity coverage ND.
DSRA
Outside opening pool; released once if debt settlement releases collateral. Not subtracted twice.
Current tax provision
Paid once in year 1; TDS 1.7929 recovered separately at scenario fraction. ₹2.2945 arrears presumed included in base and added only in bear overlap sensitivity.
Benefits provision
Opening net provision cash-funded once; annual wage costs include future accruals. Note actuarial amount.3321 discrepancy retained separately.
Prepaid student training fees

Annual report PDF p 140, Note 17 explicitly calls this an advance PAID and classifies it as an asset. Added to ONWC, not a customer deposit liability. Related counterparty perspective remains a disclosure reconciliation gap.
Trade payables and other current liabilities
Embedded in opening ONWC; subsequent delta ONWC handles settlement, not separate deduction.
Contingent Big Charter guarantee
Not funded debt; full call in bear year 2, zero in base/bull. Recovery zero.
Contingent TDS demand
Paid once in bear/base conservatively; cannot assume overlap with provision, sensitivity isolates risk.
Capital advances and aircraft advance
Already paid March assets; excluded as cash and not deducted again. Future project budget is unspent amount only.
Unspent IPO machine budget
Not extra cash; part of opening bank/FD pool. Approved purpose permits project use. Stub project spend deducted from both cash and remaining budget once.
Associate and property

No future equity-accounted profit or property rental income included in operating EBITDA/cash; all other income is excluded. Property is separate investment property in annual Note 12, not operating PPE. Scenario terminal asset realizations added once. Associated liabilities captured only via net asset value.
RPT loans
No opening cash credit; only bull collects 25% once in year 3, with zero terminal residual. Disclosure mismatch prevents treating balance as cash-equivalent.
Lease commitments

10-year operating leases; annual cash rentals expensed. No owned simulator purchase added and no PV lease debt deducted on top of post-rent terminal EV. Renewal and remaining-term risk in multiple/FX stress.
Dividends
None; all cash retained, so no dividend double count.
Unascertainable litigation
Not valued as zero risk. Unquantified exposure is one reason this model cannot yield a supported R or IAS.
